newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Central Bank aims to boost gold reserves.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Central Bank aims to boost gold reserves.

text.p: Russia's Central Bank aims over 1997 and 1998 to increase its gold reserves by 90 tonnes a year, Interfax news agency quoted the bank's deputy chairman, Sergei Aleksashenko, as saying on Wednesday.
He was also quoted as saying that the Bank was in a position to buy gold from commercial banks in volumes ranging from 100 kg to one tonne.

The Central Bank said at the end of January that the Bank's gold reserves were around 400 tonnes. State strategic reserves, kept at Goskhran (the former Gosfond), were nearly depleted, since they had been bought by the Central Bank.
Aleksashenko said that Central Bank coffers held over 90 percent of Russia's total gold reserves.

He said that the Bank would remain the sole buyer of gold for the next few years, adding that before the precious metals market could be liberalised, further development of Russia's gold, silver and platinum markets was needed.
Aleksashenko also said that the export of gold by commercial banks was "unreasonable" for the time being and that Russia did not expect internal gold demand to rise soon.
